## Overlap with #33808

I compared this PR against [#33808](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/33808) (same issue, #33812). Here's the exact breakdown:

### Identical / equivalent (web app)

Both PRs fix the same root cause in `packages/app/src/pages/session.tsx`:

| Change | #33808 | #35008 |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Remove `if (followup.paused[sessionID]) return` from the auto-send effect | yes | yes |
| Stop setting `followup.paused` on Esc abort | yes (`onAbort: undefined`) | yes (omit `onAbort` prop) |

Functionally the same: Esc only interrupts the current turn; queued follow-ups resume via the existing idle auto-send path.

### Only in #33808

- `packages/app/src/pages/session/composer/session-composer-region.tsx` — makes `onAbort` optional and passes `onAbort: undefined` through the composer region props.

On current `dev`, follow-up wiring goes through `createSessionComposerRegionController` + `PromptInput` directly (no `onAbort` on composer region), so that file may already be obsolete relative to this branch. If #33808 merges first, this PR shouldn't need that hunk.

### Only in #35008

- `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run/runtime.queue.ts` — `bindInterrupt` aborts the active turn's `AbortController`
- `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run/runtime.ts` — call `abortActiveTurn` before `session.abort` on Esc
- `packages/opencode/test/cli/run/runtime.queue.test.ts` — test that aborting the active signal still drains the next queued prompt

This is the **direct CLI mode** (`opencode run`) path: interrupt previously only hit the server abort API and could leave the local prompt queue stuck with a queued message visible in the footer.

### Not covered by either PR

- Legacy TUI (`packages/tui`) — separate interrupt/queue behavior; see also #34530
- Server-side `delivery: "queue"` promotion after interrupt (core session runner)

### Suggested path for maintainers

1. **If only the web app fix is wanted:** #33808 is sufficient for the app; this PR could be narrowed to CLI-only (+ test) on top of that.
2. **If both app + CLI matter:** this PR is a superset; merging it would subsume #33808's `session.tsx` changes (composer-region hunk may still be worth pulling from #33808 if that refactor lands separately).

Test screenshots attached in thread. Local verification:
- `bun test test/cli/run/runtime.queue.test.ts` — 17 pass
- `bun typecheck` in `packages/opencode`

**Scope update:** dropped the duplicate `packages/app` follow-up fix — #33808 already covers that surface.

This PR is now **CLI-only** (`opencode run`):

- `bindInterrupt` aborts the active turn's local `AbortSignal` (not just server `session.abort`)
- pending queue depth exposed for the interrupt handler
- footer shows `interrupting · N queued` when Esc fires with prompts waiting
- test asserts pending count + queued prompt still drains after abort

Stacks on #33808 for #33812. Happy to rebase once that lands.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #20695: Memory Megathread — the central tracking issue for all memory/resource usage reports. The maintainers are actively investigating and have instructions for collecting heap snapshots that would help diagnose your specific case.
- #30126: High CPU and Memory usage on macOS ARM64 (similar symptoms)
- #22548: OpenCode and bun using way more resources (similar report)
- #29671: Startup deadlock, single-core 100% CPU utilization, and severe memory leak on Linux

In particular, please follow the instructions in #20695 to collect a heap snapshot — that is the most useful data the team can use to track down the root cause. You can trigger it with:
```
OPENCODE_AUTO_HEAP_SNAPSHOT=1 opencode
```
Use it until memory grows, then upload the generated `.heapsnapshot` file as described in #20695.

# Report: "Open Project" collapses two clones of the same repo

## Symptom
When two independent clones of the same repo live in different folders
(e.g. `~/myrepo.branchA` and `~/myrepo.branchB`), opening the second folder via
**Open Project** routes to the already-open first project instead of opening a
separate project instance.

## Reproduction path in code
When you invoke **Open Project** (menu item `project.open` in
`packages/app/src/desktop-menu.ts:102`, or the **+** button in
`packages/app/src/pages/layout/sidebar-shell.tsx:80`), both routes land in
`chooseProject()` → `openProject(directory)` in
`packages/app/src/pages/layout.tsx`, which calls
**`layout.projects.open(directory)`**. That's where the short-circuit lives.

## The short-circuit (the check in question)
`packages/app/src/context/layout.tsx:614`

```ts
projects: {
  list,
  open(directory: string) {
    const root = rootFor(directory)                                     // ← collapses branchB → branchA
    if (server.projects.list().find((x) => x.worktree === root)) return // ← short-circuits, shows existing
    void serverSync().project.loadSessions(root)
    server.projects.open(root)
  },
```

There is a second, lower-level guard at `packages/app/src/context/server.tsx:79`:

```ts
open(directory: string) {
  const scope = input.scope()
  if (current().some((project) => project.worktree === directory)) return
  ...
```

Note: **`server.tsx:79` already compares by exact folder path**
(`worktree === directory`) — that one is fine. The problem is upstream: by the
time we get there, `directory` has already been rewritten from branchB's path to
branchA's path by `rootFor()`.

## Why `rootFor()` rewrites the path — the actual culprit
`packages/app/src/context/layout.tsx:454-485`

- `roots()` (line 454) builds a `Map<sandbox → worktree>` from every project's
  `sandboxes` array:
  ```ts
  map.set(sandbox, project.worktree)
  ```
- `rootFor(directory)` (line 465) walks that map: if the folder you passed
  appears as a *sandbox* of an already-open project, it returns that project's
  `worktree` instead of your folder.

So the moment `~/myrepo.branchB` is registered as a **sandbox** of the branchA
project, `rootFor("~/myrepo.branchB")` returns `~/myrepo.branchA`, and the
`find(x => x.worktree === root)` check on line 618 matches — you get routed to
branchA.

## Why branchB becomes a "sandbox" of branchA — the root cause
Two things combine:

1. **Project identity is repo-based, not folder-based.**
   `packages/core/src/project.ts:110` `resolve()` computes the project `id` as:
   git-remote hash → else root-commit hash → else cached id. Two separate clones
   of the same repo share the same remote and same root commit, so they get the
   **same project id**.

2. **The backend then files the second folder under the first project as a
   sandbox.** `packages/opencode/src/project/project.ts:241-246`:
   ```ts
   if (
     projectID !== ProjectV2.ID.global &&
     data.directory !== result.worktree &&          // branchB path != branchA's stored worktree
     !result.sandboxes.includes(data.directory)
   )
     result.sandboxes.push(data.directory)          // ← branchB added as a sandbox of branchA
   ```
   Because `resolve()` returned branchA's existing DB row (same id),
   `result.worktree` is branchA's path while `data.directory` is branchB's path,
   so branchB is pushed into `sandboxes` and persisted. That's what later feeds
   `roots()`/`rootFor()` on the frontend.

## Summary — where "same repo" needs to also mean "same folder"

| Layer | File / symbol | Line | Role in the bug |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frontend open handler | `layout.projects.open` — `packages/app/src/context/layout.tsx` | 616-621 | Short-circuits after `rootFor()` rewrites branchB→branchA |
| Frontend path rewrite | `rootFor` / `roots` — `packages/app/src/context/layout.tsx` | 454-485 | Maps sandbox folder back to root worktree (the collapse) |
| Frontend low-level guard | `open` — `packages/app/src/c

## Additional investigation: root cause is an eager ModelsDev refresh logging before the OpenCode logger is installed

I reproduced the stdout leak locally and traced the likely cause.

### Summary

`ModelsDev.node` starts an eager background `refresh()` during layer construction. When `https://models.dev/api.json` is unavailable, that refresh logs `Failed to fetch models.dev` with `Effect.logError(...)`.

If that log runs before OpenCode's `Observability.layer` logger has been installed, Effect's default logger writes to **stdout**. In the TUI, stdout is owned by OpenTUI, so the log text is rendered into the terminal frame and corrupts the UI.

Providing `Observability.layer` before building `ModelsDev.node` prevents the stdout write in the minimal repro.

### Relevant code paths

- `packages/core/src/models-dev.ts`
  - `refresh()` logs the fetch failure:
    ```ts
    Effect.tapCause((cause) => Effect.logError("Failed to fetch models.dev", { cause: cause })),
    Effect.ignore,
    ```
  - the service forks an eager refresh during layer construction:
    ```ts
    yield* Effect.forkScoped(refresh().pipe(Effect.repeat(Schedule.spaced("60 minutes")), Effect.ignore))
    ```
- `packages/core/src/observability/logging.ts`
  - OpenCode's logger writes to the log file by default and to stderr only with `OPENCODE_PRINT_LOGS=1`.
  - If this logger is not installed yet, Effect's built-in/default logger is used instead.
- `packages/tui/src/app.tsx`
  - the TUI renderer uses stdout for the terminal UI, so any accidental stdout log can visually corrupt the frame.

### Minimal repro evidence

Working tree/tag used for investigation:

- `v1.17.13` / `10c894bdee`
- current `origin/dev` checked separately at `5455fed78e`; `packages/core/src/models-dev.ts` is effectively unchanged for this behavior.

First, Effect's default logger writes errors to stdout:

```sh
cd packages/core
bun -e 'import { Effect } from "effect"; Effect.runSync(Effect.logError("probe-error"));' \
  > /tmp/effect-log.out 2> /tmp/effect-log.err
wc -c < /tmp/effect-log.out
wc -c < /tmp/effect-log.err
cat /tmp/effect-log.out
```

Observed:

```text
stdout bytes: 39
stderr bytes: 0
[02:48:03.737] ERROR (#1): probe-error
```

Then a minimal `ModelsDev.node` build with a failing mock HTTP client reproduces the same stdout leak:

```ts
import { Effect, Layer } from "effect"
import { HttpClient, HttpClientResponse } from "effect/unstable/http"
import { AppNodeBuilder } from "@opencode-ai/core/effect/app-node-builder"
import { LayerNodePlatform } from "@opencode-ai/core/effect/app-node-platform"
import { Flag } from "@opencode-ai/core/flag/flag"
import { ModelsDev } from "@opencode-ai/core/models-dev"

await Effect.runPromise(Effect.gen(function* () {
  Flag.OPENCODE_MODELS_URL = "https://offline.invalid"
  Flag.OPENCODE_MODELS_PATH = undefined
  Flag.OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH = false

  const client = HttpClient.make((request) =>
    Effect.succeed(HttpClientResponse.fromWeb(request, Response.error())),
  )

  const layer = Layer.fresh(AppNodeBuilder.build(ModelsDev.node, [
    [LayerNodePlatform.httpClient, Layer.succeed(HttpClient.HttpClient, client)],
  ]))

  yield* Layer.build(layer)
  yield* Effect.sleep("100 millis")
}).pipe(Effect.scoped))
```

Observed when redirecting streams:

```text
models stdout bytes: 135
models stderr bytes: 0
[02:48:04.307] ERROR (#14): Failed to fetch models.dev {
  cause: {
    _id: "Cause",
    failures: [
      [Object ...]
    ],
  },
}
```

Control case: if the same layer is built with `Observability.layer` provided first, the repro produces no stdout/stderr leak:

```ts
yield* Layer.build(modelsLayer.pipe(Layer.provideMerge(Observability.layer)))
yield* Effect.sleep("100 millis")
```

Observed:

```text
observed stdout bytes: 0
observed stderr bytes: 0
```
